source_method: Modern FNA genus/species treatments and regional secondary floras; all evidence scope and incomplete traits recorded explicitly; 1999 flora has no direct treatment for these taxa.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Carphochaete genus treatment (D. J. Keil), vol. 21 pp. 460, 486
sources.evidence_scope: genus circumscription; only USA species in treatment

sources.reference: Texas Wild Buds, Carphochaete bigelovii species description

morphology.habit: Woody-based subshrub, typically erect and branched; genus (8–)20–45(–120+) cm with greater extremes across wider genus
morphology.leaves: Opposite (occasional alternate in genus), sessile narrow elliptic/oblanceolate to linear, 1–3-nerved and conspicuously gland-pitted
morphology.heads: Discoid, often single or paired, with approximately 3–6 white/pinkish-purple florets in cylindrical involucres
morphology.fruit: Cypselae 8–10-ribbed with long aristate pappus scales; genus also can have shorter scales

issues: Species-specific phyllary and pappus measurements not verified from full FNA species account; exclude genus-wide ranges from species diagnosis.
Potential location/identity concern: do not use as evidence of Hays County occurrence.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Ericameria nauseosa species and key
USFS Fire Effects Information System, Ericameria nauseosa
National Park Service, Trees and Shrubs field account

morphology.habit: Woody rubber rabbitbrush shrub/subshrub; FNA recognizes numerous variable forms
morphology.leaves: Alternate very narrow mostly single-veined blades, commonly tomentose and/or resin-gland dotted; size, hairiness and color vary strikingly among varieties
morphology.heads: Many small yellow discoid heads clustered at stem ends; approximately five disk florets per head in FNA key
morphology.involucres: About 6–14 mm high in NPS field account; often cylindric and phyllaries aligned in vertical rows
morphology.fruit: Asteraceae ribbed cypsela and capillary bristle pappus; precise species measurements unverified

issues: Do not assign one infraspecific leaf width or pubescence condition to all E. nauseosa.
Texas nativity and Hays-target status remain unverified.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Eriophyllum lanatum species treatment

morphology.habit: Perennial herb or subshrub commonly 10–100 cm; sometimes flowers in first year
morphology.leaves: Alternate at least proximally; variable entire or lobed, conspicuously woolly underside in many forms; substantial varietal variation
morphology.heads: Yellow radiate heads single or in small clusters of 2–5 or more; FNA key reports ray flowers 0 or 5–13(–15)
morphology.involucres: 6–15 mm diameter across broad species key, not a variety diagnosis
morphology.fruit: Cypselae with reduced pappus scales/crown, detailed measurements need specific variety

issues: Western species complex with ten FNA varieties; do not derive local Texas eligibility from this broad treatment.
Species-level source broad, subspecific features unverified.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Gaillardia amblyodon species treatment
Flora of North America, Gaillardia genus key

morphology.habit: Annual herb (requires full species account for species-specific stem dimensions)
morphology.rays: Usually uniform dark red to purple, rarely yellow (FNA key)
morphology.disks: Disk corolla lobes mostly ovate-deltate to lanceolate, 0.5–1 mm (FNA key)
morphology.fruits: Dimorphic cypselae: outer longer than inner with shorter pappus scales, according to key
morphology.heads: Gaillardia heads solitary and radiate/discoid depending on species; this taxon normally with conspicuous rays

issues: FNA explicitly says G. amblyodon may not prove distinct from G. pulchella at species rank.
Preserve as distinct repository record but hold any final photo/identification approval pending evidence.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Gymnosperma genus treatment
Felger and Rutman, Ajo Peak to Tinajas Altas flora, Part 21 Asteraceae

morphology.habit: Taprooted strongly resinous shrub, FNA 50–150(–200) cm; southwest field flora often 0.6–1 m
morphology.stems: New growth often visibly sticky from glandular/resinous exudate
morphology.leaves: Small sessile aromatic resinous leaves, more detailed dimensions require full species treatment
morphology.heads: Dense terminal corymbiform clusters of minute heads with very inconspicuous rays
morphology.fruit: Cypselae with no pappus, a distinctive genus character

issues: Monotypic genus makes FNA genus diagnosis relevant; still retain source scope explicitly.
Not evidence of target county nativity.

sources.reference: World Flora Online, Parthenium confertum species page (FNA morphology)
Flora of North America, Parthenium confertum

morphology.habit: Biennial, sometimes flowering first year or persisting; stems 10–30(–60+) cm
morphology.leaves: Lobed to pinnately divided, undersides finely strigillose and often with longer erect hairs ~1–2 mm
morphology.heads: Small disciform or only obscurely radiate heads in loose panicle-like branching arrays
morphology.flowers: Minute pistillate rays and tubular disks; genus character, exact flower counts pending full species treatment

issues: Do not borrow the deeply twice-pinnatifid leaf morphology from P. hysterophorus.
Fruit and phyllary measurements not established from visible source excerpts.
